title: Beer-drinking parties, buck dancing and shows with his brother in Arkansas
summary: He and his brother played guitar and sang for local parties for fun, then put on shows with paid admission in Jennings and Chico.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Well, did you play at dances, picnics and things like that?

We played for -- they call -- back there in those days they would have what you call a beer drinking parties and when they had the beer drinking parties, funny thing, they wouldn't exclude -- they wouldn't -- kids wasn't allowed. We didn't fool with beer -- we didn't drink the beer, we just go for the music, and everyone know that the Randolph kids played the guitar, so they'd ask me and my brother. So we would play -- practically be the music part.
I see.
Yes.
Did you get any pay for that or was it just for fun?

Fun. Me and my brother -- just fun. We'd go in there and it'd tickle us. You know, we was just glad to get to play. And now, it's a funny thing. I don't know if you've heard about this dancing or not. They call it
buck dancing.
Yes.
Yes. Buck dancing and what you would have to play --
(music)

That chord -- let me see. And he's cutting all kind of -- and sometimes while this is going on he's talking. And he's really talking and dancing all at the same time. That's what my brother would be doing when we put on these shows. We'd put these shows on and when one would sing we would have to play the accompaniment, play the accompaniment and each -- well, sometimes we would have duets together and I would have to sing the second part and he would sing the lead.
Did he play guitar also?
My brother?
I mean, would you play guitar duets?
No, we didn't play --
You would play guitar and he would sing and then sometimes both of you would sing.
And then sometimes he'd take the guitar and then we'd sing.
I see.
Of course, we only had one guitar.
Were there a lot of -- this was in a rural part of Arkansas, wasn't it?

Yes. This was in a little small town. One place called Chico, Arkansas, that we stayed in. All over Arkansas in a way of speaking. Then we stayed in a place called Jennings, Arkansas, and that's where we put on our shows, in Jennings, Arkansas. We put those shows on and people would come to them. Now, our audience was integrated at times.
Yes.
And --
This is other than the beer drinking parties? This is where you and your brother would charge admission to the shows?

Yes. Of course, we'd grown up and were a little older then. About 11 years old, 11 and 12. And I never will forget it, the year of the Titanic, that was 1912, you know, that's when the Titanic went down.
